Entries.Message: Possible null pointer dereference: readback
Entries.Assessment: False positive: Require throws on failed DiagnosticCpuReadback::Create; successful factory publishes a non-null candidate only after starting the worker. Every failure preserves output. Existing allocation/error-path and real worker tests exercise this contract.

Entries.Message: Function 'GetSnapshot()' should return member 'snapshot_' by const reference.
Entries.Assessment: Re-confirmed against the Step 09 Encoder telemetry revision; the finding and its verdict are unchanged. Deliberate value observation: returning a reference would let callers alias the tracker mutable snapshot across later Bind, Observe, Reset, or stall updates. The small fixed record is copied to preserve point-in-time semantics; progress boundary, stall, and reset tests cover it.

Entries.Message: Technically the member function 'pbapp::RunEvidenceJournal::Append' can be const.
Entries.Assessment: False positive from shallow unique_ptr analysis: the analyzer does not follow mutation through the owned implementation pointer, so it reads a body that only writes the pointee as const-capable. Making the member const would be misleading and would not prevent the state change. Append appends a framed record through *implementation_, updates snapshot_ bytesWritten/samples and flips valid/truncated on failure; the cadence, byte-cap and malformed-record tests in tests/PBApplication/test_run_report.cpp rely on those transitions.

Entries.Message: Technically the member function 'pbapp::RunEvidenceJournal::Finish' can be const.
Entries.Assessment: False positive from shallow unique_ptr analysis: the analyzer does not follow mutation through the owned implementation pointer, so it reads a body that only writes the pointee as const-capable. Making the member const would be misleading and would not prevent the state change. Finish flushes and closes the journal handle through *implementation_ and sets snapshot_ finished/truncated/bytesWritten; the duration-cap and close-failure tests in tests/PBApplication/test_run_report.cpp rely on it.

Entries.Message: Technically the member function 'pbdemodd3d11::CaptureDemodulator::TakeResult' can be const.
Entries.Assessment: Re-confirmed against the current file revision after the remote-visual transport work changed this file; the finding and its verdict are unchanged. False positive from shallow unique_ptr analysis: TakeResult advances the bounded ring head, decrements queued state, increments resultsTaken, and writes the caller output. A const queue consumer would misstate thread-safety and ownership.

Entries.Message: Technically the member function 'pbdemodd3d11::Demodulator::RetireAfterExternalCompletion' can be const.
Entries.Assessment: Re-confirmed against the current file revision after the remote-visual transport work changed this file; the finding and its verdict are unchanged. It must not be callable through a const demodulator.

Entries.Message: Technically the member function 'pbdemodd3d11::Demodulator::Shutdown' can be const.
Entries.Assessment: Re-confirmed against the current file revision after the remote-visual transport work changed this file; the finding and its verdict are unchanged. Entries.Message: Technically the member function 'pbrealcapturereplay::ReplayWriter::Finalize' can be const.
Entries.Assessment: Re-confirmed against the current file revision after the remote-visual transport work changed this file; the finding and its verdict are unchanged. False positive from shallow unique_ptr analysis: Finalize writes and flushes the footer, closes the partial file, publishes the final path and changes writer state. It must not be callable through a const writer.

Entries.Message: Technically the member function 'pbrealcapturereplay::ReplayV2Writer::AppendCapture' can be const.
Entries.Assessment: False positive from shallow unique_ptr analysis: the analyzer does not follow mutation through the owned implementation pointer, so it reads a body that only writes the pointee as const-capable. Making the member const would be misleading and would not prevent the state change. AppendCapture writes the record through *implementation_ (stream CRC/digest, fileBytes, captureFrames/records, handle position) and enforces the frame and byte limits; tests/PBRealCaptureReplay/test_replay_v2.cpp covers append, limit-rejection and failure latching.

Entries.Message: Technically the member function 'pbrealcapturereplay::ReplayV2Writer::AppendDemodObservation' can be const.
Entries.Assessment: False positive from shallow unique_ptr analysis: the analyzer does not follow mutation through the owned implementation pointer, so it reads a body that only writes the pointee as const-capable. Making the member const would be misleading and would not prevent the state change. AppendDemodObservation writes a record through *implementation_ and sets capture->hasDemodObservation plus demodObservations/records/fileBytes, which is what makes a second observation for one capture fail closed; tests/PBRealCaptureReplay/test_replay_v2.cpp covers it.

Entries.Message: Technically the member function 'pbrealcapturereplay::ReplayV2Writer::Finalize' can be const.
Entries.Assessment: False positive from shallow unique_ptr analysis: the analyzer does not follow mutation through the owned implementation pointer, so it reads a body that only writes the pointee as const-capable. Making the member const would be misleading and would not prevent the state change. Finalize writes the footer, closes the handle and sets complete/fileBytes through *implementation_; the empty-session, footer and reopen-verification tests in tests/PBRealCaptureReplay/test_replay_v2.cpp cover it.

Entries.Message: Condition 'pixelsResult' is always true
Entries.Assessment: Dead defensive branch, not a defect: line 238 already returns PixelLimitExceeded when the checked product is absent, so the ternary at line 242 can never take the empty branch. It keeps the byte-limit expression free of an unchecked Value() call on the path the analyzer sees; tests/PBRemoteVisualSimulator/test_channel_transform.cpp covers the pixel, byte and work limits.

Entries.Message: Parameter 'current' can be declared as reference to const
Entries.Assessment: False positive: the mutation happens through a non-const pointer obtained from the parameter (std::vector::data() / a serialization call), which the analyzer does not attribute to the parameter. Declaring it const would be impossible, not merely wrong. ApplyBlockReplacement memcpy's into current.pixels.data() and only reads rowPitch; making it const would delete the transform. tests/PBRemoteVisualSimulator/test_channel_transform.cpp asserts the replaced block bytes.

Entries.Message: Parameter 'image' can be declared as reference to const
Entries.Assessment: False positive: the mutation happens through a non-const pointer obtained from the parameter (std::vector::data() / a serialization call), which the analyzer does not attribute to the parameter. Declaring it const would be impossible, not merely wrong. ApplyColorTransfer rewrites every pixel through image.pixels.data() row by row; the limited-range and full-range assertions in tests/PBRemoteVisualSimulator/test_channel_transform.cpp fail if the write does not happen.

Entries.Message: Parameter 'image' can be declared as reference to const
Entries.Assessment: False positive: the mutation happens through a non-const pointer obtained from the parameter (std::vector::data() / a serialization call), which the analyzer does not attribute to the parameter. Declaring it const would be impossible, not merely wrong. ApplySolidOverlay blends in place through image.pixels.data(); the overlay byte assertions in tests/PBRemoteVisualSimulator/test_channel_transform.cpp cover the write path.

Entries.Message: Function 'GetSnapshot()' should return member 'snapshot_' by const reference.
Entries.Assessment: Deliberate value snapshot: the fixed counter record is copied so callers cannot alias mutable accumulator state or retain a reference across later observations. Returning a reference would weaken snapshot lifetime and immutability.

Entries.Message: Parameter 'output' can be declared as const array
Entries.Assessment: False positive: the mutation happens through a non-const pointer obtained from the parameter (std::vector::data() / a serialization call), which the analyzer does not attribute to the parameter. Declaring it const would be impossible, not merely wrong. output is the caller-owned Bootstrap record buffer filled by pbprotocol::SerializeBootstrapRecord; a const buffer could not receive the serialization, and tests/tools/test_remote_visual_receiver_evidence.cpp checks the produced record bytes.
